primary.title: Morning Brief
selectionRules: choose the newest valid issue in the active window
prefer the newest same-day issue in the configured timezone when one exists

groups.title: Main article
notes: Explain the lead story clearly and with concrete detail.

groups.title: Other major stories
notes: Each bullet should describe what happened and why it matters.
Do not use headline fragments as bullets.

primary.title: Business Brief
selectionRules: choose the newest valid issue in the active window
prefer the newest same-day issue in the configured timezone when one exists
if sender formatting changes, match using sender variants, subject, publication, and body clues

groups.title: Opener
notes: Keep the opener as its own labeled section.

specialCases.name: Single-feature edition
specialCases.trigger: one main feature instead of the usual opener-plus-multiple-story format
notes: Do not fabricate recurring sections when the source does not support them.

primary.title: Technology Brief
selectionRules: choose the newest valid issue in the active window
prefer the newest same-day issue in the configured timezone when one exists

groups.title: Roundup
notes: Each bullet should be 1-2 descriptive sentences.
Choose the most important items rather than trying to include everything.

extras.title: Independent Review
itemRules: Include one bullet per included item.
Start with the publication name when available.
Use a separate link field when available.
Write a 2-3 sentence summary in plain text.

extras.title: Research Updates
extras.linkPreference: useful public article page when one exists
itemRules: Include one bullet per included item.
Use a separate link field when available.
Write a 1-2 sentence summary in plain text.

generalSelectionRules: always do a historical pull; do not rely only on webhook or new-mail state
first fetch metadata/snippets for the lookback window, then fetch full bodies only for selected messages
use a strict 36-hour cutoff from the run start time; reject messages older than the configured lookback window even when Gmail query hints overfetch
fallback matching may broaden sender, subject, publication, and body clues, but must never broaden the configured lookback window
